page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is an entry-level, memory-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM. Running on a KVM hypervisor with the x86_64 architecture, the instance allocates two hardware threads across a single physical core of an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The CPU subsystem features 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES instructions. The configuration does not include local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware.

Benchmark results reflect entry-level performance characteristics defined by the dual-vCPU ceiling. In synthetic processor workloads, the instance recorded a Geekbench single-core score of 981.0 and a multi-core score of 1743.0, alongside a PassMark CPU score of 2616.1. Stress-ng returned 1102.08 for single-core and 2162.17 for multi-core throughput. Memory bandwidth tests demonstrated 17.2 GB/sec for uncached read-only streams and 14.52 GB/sec for large block writes. Application-level throughput reached 2.52 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and 2.49 GB/sec in static web serving benchmarks.

With an 8 GB RAM per vCPU ratio, the system offers high memory density relative to its processing capacity. This design suits workloads that demand in-memory capacity over raw CPU compute throughput, such as lightweight Redis or Memcached instances, staging environments, low-traffic database backends, and simple background job processing queues. Workloads requiring sustained high computational throughput or intensive local storage I/O require scaling to instances with higher core counts or dedicated local NVMe disks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.e3.medium is a memory-oriented virtual instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor operating at 2.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The virtual machine delivers 2 vCPUs derived from a single physical core via hyper-threading, accompanied by 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. It does not include integrated local storage or GPU acceleration. In benchmark evaluations, the instance produced a Geekbench multi-core score of 1743.0, a PassMark CPU score of 2616.1, and an uncached memory read bandwidth of 17.2 GB/sec. Application testing yielded 2.52 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks. The hardware profile is well suited for memory-centric, low-compute workloads including intermediate caching tiers, low-volume database services, and general background application staging.
